external_entities.name: colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues who sign in through the identity broker and use applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
external_entities.notes: Tokens carry each colleague's staff id and group memberships.

external_entities.name: franchise colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues from franchise stores who authenticate through their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The source does not state which franchise colleagues the identity provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: An identity provider controlled by the franchise that vouches for franchise colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, signs tokens, maintains directory membership, and writes audit records.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The broker does not receive callbacks to check whether a colleague is still allowed in. It pulls HR changes once a night; leavers stop being colleagues through that process. Tokens are valid for twelve hours and cannot be revoked before expiry. The source does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses token groups to authorize changing prices and voiding transactions across stores.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications. It also runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: A store-manager token works against every store because the console does not check which store the colleague belongs to.

processes.name: HR system
processes.description: The system that supplies colleague group-membership changes to the identity broker overnight.
processes.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the identity broker for tokens.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory of colleagues and their groups.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. Nobody has written down whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: Colleagues sign in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token carrying the colleague's staff ID and groups.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in.
data_flows.data_description: token containing staff id and group memberships

data_flows.name: present token
data_flows.description: Colleagues present the broker-issued token to the store admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.data_description: broker-issued token with staff id and group memberships

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the broker's signing key.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: send membership changes
data_flows.description: The HR system sends colleague group-membership changes to the identity broker overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night

data_flows.name: update directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains colleague and group data in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker reads its token-signing key from the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_flows.notes: The same key signs tokens for every application.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.

data_flows.name: franchise sign-in
data_flows.description: Franchise colleagues sign in through the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.
data_flows.notes: The source says franchise colleagues use their own identity provider, but does not describe the direct interaction in further detail.

data_flows.name: vouch for colleague
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for franchise colleagues to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: home devices
trust_boundaries.description: Colleagues' own devices at home from which they sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

assumptions.assumption: The key store contains confidential data because it holds the token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store holds the broker's signing key; signing keys are secrets.

assumptions.assumption: The directory contains confidential data because it holds colleague identities and group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory holds colleagues and the groups they are in; these are personal and access-control data.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log contains confidential data because it holds sign-in records.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log; sign-in records describe identifiable colleagues.
